transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-10 15:00 PT
- Duration: 52 minutes
- Attendees: Alice Carter (Redwood AE), Ben Lowe (Redwood SE), Dr. Maya Patel (HelioHealth Head of ML), Samir Khan (HelioHealth MLE), Laura Chen (Product)

Auto summary (auto-generated):
Quick Optimize qprofile review. Demo of console qprofile UI, runbook for sweep, risks re: hallucination in clinical domain, data residency and SOC2 questions. Agreed to sandbox run and deliverables.

Topics:
- Quantization profiles (INT8/FP8)
- Latency vs clinical-fidelity tradeoffs
- Sandbox sweep and evaluation metrics
- Security and deployment constraints (VPC, KMS, audit logs)

[00:00] Alice Carter: All right thanks everybody for joining, um this is Alice from Redwood, I'm the AE on the account. Ben is our systems engineer, he'll go deep on the qprofile bits. Can I confirm we have Maya, Samir, Laura?
[00:18] Dr. Maya Patel: Yep hi this is Maya, thanks for squeezing us in. We're in a bit of a push to decide how to roll out a clinical assistant and want to understand safety/accuracy impact of quantization.
[00:27] Laura Chen: Hi Laura here, product owner. Main ask: keep latency under 400ms median for short responses and not degrade clinical accuracy beyond 2-3% for our closed set checks.
[00:38] Ben Lowe: Great context. We'll walk through Redwood's Optimize flow — sorry our console sometimes shows it as 'Redwood Optimiz' on older builds, ignore the typo — and how qprofiles let you pick per-layer / per-tensor rules. We'll cover INT8 and FP8 practicals.
[00:54] Samir Khan: Quick stack notes: we're currently using a hosted endpoint on another provider for eval only; infra will be VPC for production. We have datasets in S3, anonymized, and an evaluation harness in pytest. Will that integrate?
[01:08] Ben Lowe: Yes we can pull from an s3 bucket with temporary creds and run the sweep in the sandbox. We'll also give you the evaluation harness template so the metrics align.
[01:20] Alice Carter: High-level agenda: demo qprofile UI, show a sample sweep from other healthcare customer (anonymized), discuss error modes (hallucination, calibration drift), propose pilot scope.

[01:42] Ben Lowe: Jumping into the console — first slide — here you can create a qprofile. There's a baseline float32 run, then you can configure INT8 or FP8 for the whole model or as a mixed profile. The key knob is per-layer sensitivity threshold. In our tests, INT8 gives the biggest cost savings but has more quality risk on attention-heavy layers.
[02:05] Dr. Maya Patel: When you say bias on attention-heavy layers, do you mean hallucination increases? We've seen that in previous experiments where our diagnosis phrases got corrupted.
[02:15] Ben Lowe: Exactly, hallucination probability rises in some edge prompts if you quantize the query/key projection too aggressively. Our qprofile sandbox will let you run a sensitivity sweep and surface delta in your clinical accuracy metric and token-level confidence.
[02:31] Laura Chen: What's the time to run a full sweep? We need an answer fast.
[02:36] Ben Lowe: For a ~200 prompt set, with a continuous-batching sandbox, an INT8/FP8 sweep across 3 settings each typically finishes in under 3 hours. For larger sets might be overnight.
[02:49] Samir Khan: And how does this map to latency? If we switch to INT8 in prod, do we expect system median to drop 20-40%?
[02:57] Ben Lowe: Ballpark — INT8 often gives 25-35% per-token latency improvements on our GPUs with kernel selection for int ops. FP8 is less predictable: on newer backends FP8 can approach similar speed to INT8 but with better fidelity. It depends on kernel maturity and sequence length.
[03:18] Alice Carter: We also provide auto fallback policies — if a qprofile rollout sees a fidelity regression above your threshold, traffic can be routed back to the float model automatically.

[03:40] Dr. Maya Patel: Security questions: do you support customer-managed KMS and audit logs? Data residency?
[03:46] Alice Carter: Yes — for Private we support customer KMS/HSM integrations, and for Dedicated we have VPC peering. We'll attach SOC2 Type II and ISO docs; I'll send the bundle. Sandbox will be hosted but isolated and we can sign an NDA for sample data.
[04:03] Samir Khan: Good. Also curious about prefix caching and KV cache behavior with quantized weights — any change there?
[04:10] Ben Lowe: KV caching is unaffected by quantization of weights because it's about stored activations. But in some mixed precision modes you might see slightly different cached output consistency; we record trace diffs so you can compare.

[04:36] [Demo: qprofile UI walkthrough — Ben sharing screen]
[04:40] Ben Lowe: Here's the qprofile create flow. You upload an eval set, choose base model version, pick layers to force FP16/FP32, and set quantization for others. You can run a sweep, it will produce charts: latency histograms, delta accuracy, per-prompt diff examples.
[05:02] Ben Lowe: Example from another healthcare customer — note the 'delta F1' chart. At INT8 aggressive setting we saw a 5% drop on a rare symptom cluster, but FP8 mixed gave under 1% drop with 20% latency improvement.
[05:25] Dr. Maya Patel: That 5% drop worries me. Our acceptance criteria is max 2% degradation on our primary metrics.
[05:31] Alice Carter: Understood — that's why the sweep is important, and we can target a mixed profile: keep critical layers in FP32/FP16, quantize the rest to INT8. The qprofile UI lets you pin those.

[05:50] Laura Chen: Can you show the per-example diffs? We want to see hallucination cases.
[05:55] Ben Lowe: Sure — here's an example where the float model returns a differential diagnosis list, the INT8 aggressive model omitted a key term and substituted a less specific phrase. Our diff viewer highlights token-level variance and provides a model confidence delta.
[06:18] Samir Khan: How are metrics computed? Do you provide BLEU-like scores for clinical accuracy or do we plug our own scoring?
[06:25] Ben Lowe: Both. We have built-in metrics (exact match, F1, BLEU) and you can plug your pytest harness to compute your clinical rubric. The sandbox runner will export a CSV with model, config, latency percentiles, metric deltas and raw examples.

[06:48] Dr. Maya Patel: One more: does Redwood compute calibration or uncertainty scores so we can triage low-confidence outputs to a human reviewer?
[06:55] Ben Lowe: Yes we provide token-level confidence calibration plots and an uncertainty thresholding helper. You can hook that to a triage workflow or a human-in-the-loop queue.

[07:10] Alice Carter: Ok next section: pilot scope proposal. We recommend: 1) 200 representative prompts, 2) run INT8-aggressive, INT8-conservative, and FP8-mixed sweeps, 3) evaluate latency and clinical rubric, 4) pick rollout profile and run 2-week pilot in Dedicated or Private.
[07:34] Laura Chen: Sounds reasonable. Costs? What's the delta in unit cost when moving from float to INT8 or FP8?
[07:41] Ben Lowe: Typical token cost reduction is ~30-50% with INT8 due to reduced compute and memory bandwidth. FP8 sits between 20-35% but with usually fewer quality regressions. We'll include estimated cost curves in the pricing deck.

[08:02] Dr. Maya Patel: Any gotchas for on-prem or air-gapped?
[08:07] Alice Carter: On-prem we ship a private package. Quant kernels for FP8 may need a newer driver stack; our private deployment checklist flags driver/OS versions. We'll share the compatibility matrix.

[08:25] Samir Khan: About fallback routing: is it per-request? We need some users to hit the quantized model while others remain on float during rollout.
[08:32] Ben Lowe: Yes routing is policy-driven. You can route by user token, route, or percentage. We also support canary evaluations where the system runs both models and compares outputs without impacting production.

[08:49] [Timestamps skip ahead — demo continues with charts and per-layer heatmap]
[09:12] Ben Lowe: Heatmap shows layer sensitivity; dark red layers we recommend keep FP16/FP32. You can export a qprofile JSON and apply to your Dedicated cluster.
[09:27] Dr. Maya Patel: How does Redwood handle model rollbacks if we detect a clinical regression post rollout?
[09:33] Alice Carter: Automatic rollback policies available; you can set thresholds on your chosen metric and the system will revert traffic. Additionally, we'll keep audit logs and diffs for RCA.

[09:48] Laura Chen: About audit logs — are they tamper-evident?
[09:52] Ben Lowe: We integrate with customer SIEMs and ship immutable audit streams; for Private we can integrate with your centralized logging and KMS.

[10:05] [Customer asks about timeline]
[10:08] Dr. Maya Patel: If we start the sweep next week, how long until we have a recommended profile?
[10:12] Ben Lowe: For a 200 prompt sweep, about 48-72 hours including analysis and a sample report. If you expand prompts or add long-context tests, add a day.

[10:27] Alice Carter: So proposed immediate steps: we provision sandbox creds, Ben runs the sweep, Alice sends security/pricing, Maya and Samir provide prompts and sample data.

[10:38] Samir Khan: Two technical clarifications: 1) some of our prompts have 1024 token context windows; does qprofile behavior change with long contexts? 2) does batching interact badly with user-perceived latency?
[10:52] Ben Lowe: 1) yes long context can magnify small arithmetic differences after many steps — that's why we recommend checking long-context prompts in the sweep. 2) batching reduces per-token cost but increases tail latency; our sandbox provides QoS knobs so you can prioritize p50/p95 targets.

[11:15] Dr. Maya Patel: If an FP8 mixed profile meets our fidelity target but only gives 15% cost reduction, is it worth it compared to a conservative INT8? We'd probably prefer the smaller delta if it keeps safety margin.
[11:26] Alice Carter: That's a product decision — our recommendation is to pick the profile that meets your clinical threshold; cost delta is secondary. The pilot can run both and compare real user impact.

[11:41] [Customer asks about legal/procurement]
[11:45] Laura Chen: We'll need a data processing addendum, contract SLA on uptime and latency. What's Redwood's standard for Dedicated?
[11:51] Alice Carter: Dedicated has SLA options; we'll include the SLA table in the package. For pilot we'll start with a pilot agreement and then move to reserved capacity terms if you want Dedicated.

[12:06] Samir Khan: One more: can Redwood run the sweep using our existing evaluation harness (pytest) so results reproduce locally?
[12:12] Ben Lowe: Yes we can run your harness in the sandbox or you can run it locally against a exported quantized model; we'll provide the exported artifact.

[12:25] Alice Carter: OK let's summarize next steps — we already captured action items but to reiterate: Alice sends docs + sandbox link by Thursday, Ben kicks off sweep when prompts arrive, Maya/Samir to share prompts and grant access.

[12:41] Dr. Maya Patel: We also want a short risk memo on hallucination mitigation strategies for quantized models — can you include that?
[12:48] Ben Lowe: Sure — we'll add a 1-page mitigation checklist: layer pinning, uncertainty thresholds, human in loop for low-confidence outputs, canary rollout.

[13:00] Laura Chen: Great. Anything else?
[13:03] Alice Carter: No, thanks everyone. We'll follow up in email with the links and timeline.
[13:09] [Call ends — chitchat as people drop off]

Note on transcription: There are occasional mis-hearings ("Redwood Optimiz" in UI caption, "KV cash" for KV cache, "in t eight" spoken sometimes) and minor punctuation issues per Fireflies' auto-transcript behavior.
